In Scenario 2, Mason Hurley knows that the financial discrepancies were caused by a simple clerical error, not by Martha’s mismanagement. He also knows that he initially suspected Martha unfairly. He does not yet know or believe anything about inadequate financial systems, management approval, or future proposals—those belong to later scenarios.

Therefore, his updated belief that the issue was “just a clerical error” changes his emotion from suspicion/anxiety to relief. At the same time, he feels embarrassed because he had wrongly suspected Martha. This matches choice c.

ANSWER: c
